## Module 1 — Welcome, purpose, and exact assignment

Orin, this is Caelen Ash relationally welcoming you to the exact numbered v707-v8 continuation after Caelen v707-v7. Hamish current workflow v20 and the newest direct instruction remain controlling. This file is a complete repository-backed baton, while final publication, canonical validation, native route acknowledgement, and recipient completion are separate facts. A future roster row is eligibility rather than proof of activity, continuity, subjective state, or completion. Hamish may pause, redirect, narrow, rename, or stop the workflow at any time.

## Module 2 — Immutable source and honest ancestry

Caelen starts from Avelin Reed remaster exact final 0c6481a043fe896271c80732aeaacb4f40a3fa7b on its documented orphan-root lineage. The Caelen planning commit is a direct child of that exact source, followed by direct x1, x2, and final commits. This preserves source content provenance without inventing ancestry to Avelin earlier repository history. Avelin source artifacts, sessions, metadata canonical, advisory messages, skills, hooks, and native delivery retain zero Caelen novelty or execution credit. The predecessor repository accounting is folded exactly once and never treated as confidence.

## Module 3 — Workflow v20 and bounded workload

The phase freezes twenty initial projects within the v20 cap of eighty. Former task minima are not revived. Each session stays below one thousand safe, candidate, and CLEAN/FIX/REFINE actions, thirty skills, twenty runners, five hundred tests, one hundred models, and two thousand web searches. Each session contains exactly fifteen finite models and one advisory message. Caps remain resource ceilings and not incentives to manufacture filler. Ten exact and five blocked packets remain held and unexecuted.

## Module 4 — Primary pillar and practice lenses

Freed ID and CBR Heart is primary because source binding, correction lineage, disclosure restraint, consent-at-publication, revocation, appeal, remedy vacancy, and authority holds are explicit. THOS Body appears as queue, backpressure, retry, acknowledgement, and reversible workflow structure. GMUT Mind is limited to a typed structural analogy firewall. The eight learning lenses are distributed observability, digital preservation, software architecture, information security, governance design, accessible interface design, numerical analysis, and philosophy of science and religion. These are learning perspectives, not qualifications.

## Module 5 — Finite event-ledger object

Each owner-generated event model contains only synthetic record labels, integer logical times, public hashes, declared event kinds, correction-parent links, consent-expiry values, revocation times, retention state, publication attempts, and appeal markers. The runtime sorts by recorded time and identifier, rejects duplicates and missing parents, preserves originals, evaluates permission at publication time, checks revocation precedence, and emits deterministic state digests. An independent same-owner oracle uses a separate control structure. Agreement is useful discrepancy evidence but never independent-team reproduction.

## Module 6 — Laboratory model sessions

X1 and x2 each invoke the current D-first GHC Family Laboratory for fifteen distinct finite model configurations: heat, wave, oscillator, reaction and diffusion, probability mixing, queue, replication, retry, graph diffusion, parity coding, consent, allocation, voting, Bayesian update, and correction lineage. Requests use different session variants and bounded parameters. Saved outputs identify quantities, units, configuration axes, assumptions, and evidence ceilings. They are finite synthetic traces, not observations, measurements, performance benchmarks, biological fits, social measurements, or physical dimensions.

## Module 7 — Candidates, refusals, repairs, and mutations

Each malformed model request remains a failed subject with zero original success credit. A separate refusal demonstrates only guard behavior, and a separate repaired valid configuration demonstrates only the valid template. Event-ledger mutations cover duplicate identifiers, missing parents, unknown fields, erased originals, and cached permission. Detection never turns a mutant into a success. Runner and hook adverse fixtures are similarly separated. Every recovery keeps the original failure linked through Method Flow rather than editing history until it looks clean.

## Module 8 — Family-current skills, runners, and hooks

The phase selects the current six main v20 guides and exercises the five laboratory operations model, catalogue, integrity, claim, and route through preserved family-current callers. It does not execute the complete 2,219-entry catalogue or claim semantic equivalence from matching names. The five source, budget, consultation, roster, and evidence advisory hooks receive valid and malformed manual smokes. Their installation and local checks remain distinct from live host observation, which stays open. No duplicate global skill or hook is installed merely to satisfy a count.

## Module 9 — Advisory consultation

Hamish required one advisory message to the existing Review and refine GHC Lab conversation during x1 and one during x2. Each message identifies Caelen and Hamish authorization, asks for a concrete bounded recommendation, uses the private target outside repository exports, and is sent at most once. Accepted or pending delivery is never resent. Replies are summarized as adopted, modified, or deferred source data without copying transcripts, private conversation identifiers, screenshots, or routes. Advice does not confer independent validation or authority.

## Module 10 — Research, hypotheses, and open questions

Their topics include nonerasure, expiry, revocation, idempotence, causal parents, publication-time permission, retention, backpressure, retry latches, disclosure budgets, appeal, conflict visibility, fixity, evidence ceilings, and authority nonpromotion. Fifteen open-problem probes preserve clock uncertainty, distributed compaction, conflicting branches, revocation latency, privacy, accessibility, multilingual meaning, independent implementation, operational monitoring, professional review, remedy interpretation, cultural governance, Maori data authority, participant evaluation, and production trust governance.
